ma_5_main_face.blurb: Main Face is one of the principal cliff sections at Crow Hill in Leominster State Forest, in central Massachusetts. Its twelve lines are almost all traditional, with a few that can also be top-roped, and they run from 5.6 up to a single 5.11. Most fall between 5.7 and 5.9, so this stretch of cliff draws plenty of moderate leaders and top-ropers. The gneiss is grainy and tends to seep, and the right-hand side stays damp longest, so the climbing season generally begins in spring once the rock has dried. Walkers use the trail along the clifftop, so a helmet is sensible.

ma_main_face_2.blurb: Main Face is the principal climbing wall at Stage Fort Park, a seaside park in Gloucester on Cape Ann, about forty minutes from Boston. It is mostly a top-rope crag on smooth, slabby granite that faces west. Twelve lines range from easy fifth class through the low 5.10s, with a couple of boulder problems and a pair of trad lines mixed in. Natural protection is thin, so most visitors rig top-ropes using slings or extra rope, with cams or nuts for anchors, and the top is easy to reach. On warm summer days the rock turns slippery and the park fills with non-climbers.

ma_upper_field.blurb: Upper Field is a small bouldering zone in Charlemont, western Massachusetts, set on the slope above the Big 45 boulder. The twelve problems lean hard: one easy slab, a few mid-range lines between roughly V3 and V6, then a cluster from V7 to V10 with several at V9. Features include a highball slab topout and a large prow jutting from an overhang near the Wild Hunt boulder. The area sits high on the hillside, around 1,600 feet. Reaching it means a short walk from the Big 45 wall, along a trail, across a clearing and up into the woods. Charlemont as a whole is young, with plenty of room for new problems.

ma_grotto_the.blurb: The Grotto is a cliff at Hanging Mountain in Sandisfield, southwestern Massachusetts, standing in a prominent spot above the talus slope. Its twelve one- and two-pitch lines are split evenly between bolted and trad, spanning 5.8 up to a single 5.12, with most of them in the 5.10s and 5.11s. The face is open and made of pale granite, and the footwork on some lines can be tricky. Rock on the mountain can be loose, so a helmet is advised, especially at the base of the wall.

ma_main_wall_3.blurb: Main Wall is the main bouldering face at Old Rusk Quarry in West Townsend, eastern Massachusetts. The wall is roughly 150 feet long, close to vertical, and tapers away at both ends, with its tallest section around 30 feet. It holds twelve problems, mostly very easy through V1, plus a few at V4 and a single V5. The quarry granite is sharp and gritty, and the left side is usually wet. Landings are uneven but manageable with pads, and broken glass around the base is a hazard.
